recognize_zh: 藍色箭頭指的是一顆脹大、顏色變淡的紅血球，裡面有多個紫紅色小點狀或小環狀的裂殖子，並夾雜棕色色素，是間日瘧（P. vivax）的裂殖體。圓圈中是一顆鐮刀狀紅血球；背景有明顯大小與形狀不一，包括淚滴狀與不規則紅血球。
features: Enlarged, pale infected red cell containing multiple small purple merozoite-like chromatin dots and small rings (schizont, blue arrow)
Fine brownish pigment granules within the infected cell
Infected cell larger than surrounding red cells, favoring P. vivax/ovale over P. falciparum
Crescent-shaped sickle cell with pointed ends (circled)
Marked anisopoikilocytosis with teardrop-like, pointed and target-like red cells
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows marked anisopoikilocytosis with teardrop-like and pointed red cells, occasional target-like forms and a sickle cell. One red cell is enlarged and pale and contains multiple chromatin dots and small ring-like merozoites with scattered brown malarial pigment, consistent with a schizont. Enlargement of the host red cell favors Plasmodium vivax. Findings are consistent with Plasmodium vivax infection in a patient with sickle cell disease; thick and thin smear parasitemia quantification and rapid antigen or PCR confirmation of species are recommended.

ddx.vs: Falciparum schizonts are rarely seen in peripheral blood, infected cells are not enlarged, and multiple delicate rings and banana-shaped gametocytes predominate.
P. ovale also enlarges red cells but typically shows oval, fimbriated host cells and schizonts with fewer (about 8) merozoites.
P. malariae infects normal-sized or small red cells and forms rosette schizonts or band forms with coarse dark pigment.
Babesia shows small pleomorphic rings and tetrad (Maltese cross) forms without pigment or schizonts.
